metaDescription: Digital marketing for Montana businesses: SEO, paid ads, social media, websites and video for Billings, Bozeman, Missoula, the Flathead and rural towns.
lead: TDM (The Digital Marketing Services) is a digital marketing agency that works remotely with Montana businesses on SEO, paid advertising, social media, websites and video. Montana is a very large state with few people, a handful of small cities far apart, and a visitor economy that swells every summer and winter. We help Montana companies reach residents across long distances and travellers before they arrive.

sections.heading: Small cities, each with its own character
paragraphs: Billings, in the south-central plains, is the largest city and the trade, medical and energy centre for eastern Montana and northern Wyoming. Bozeman has a state university, a technology and outdoor-brand community, and sits on the road to Yellowstone and Big Sky; it has grown quickly and become expensive. Missoula is a university town with a strong arts scene and healthcare employers.

Great Falls has an Air Force base and serves the farm country of the north-central part of the state. Helena is the capital. Kalispell and Whitefish, in the Flathead Valley, are the gateway to Glacier National Park and a ski resort. Butte carries a long mining history. None of these places is close to another, so a business usually serves one of them and the rural area around it.

sections.heading: Two economies: residents and visitors
paragraphs: Year-round Montana lives on ranching, wheat, energy, healthcare, construction and trades. Customers are practical, often know the owner, and will drive hours for equipment, a specialist doctor or a big shopping trip. Montana has no general sales tax, which also brings shoppers in from neighbouring states for larger purchases.

The other economy arrives from outside. In summer, travellers come for Yellowstone, Glacier, fly fishing and guest ranches. In winter they come to ski. Autumn brings hunters. These customers choose from another state, weeks or months ahead, using search, maps, reviews and video. Guides, outfitters, lodges and restaurants in gateway towns need to be found at that planning stage, not when the visitor is already in the valley.
bullets: Visitor campaigns timed to when trips are booked, well before the season opens.
Listings and hours updated for shoulder seasons, when many businesses close or cut back.
Content that answers trip-planning questions: road access, what to bring, when to come.
Separate messages for locals and visitors where a business serves both.

sections.heading: Distance and the short working season
paragraphs: A service area in Montana can cover several counties. Search results in small towns have few competitors, so a complete business profile, a handful of honest reviews and a site that names the towns you travel to can put a company at the top of the map for a wide region.

Winter is long, and building, roofing, paving and landscaping are squeezed into the warm months. Contractors are often booked out early, so their marketing matters most in late winter and spring, and many use the quiet season to fix the website and gather reviews. Heating, plumbing and snow services run the opposite way.

sections.heading: Montana brands that sell beyond Montana
paragraphs: The state's name carries weight with buyers elsewhere. Makers of outdoor gear, food products, leather goods, furniture and art sell to customers around the country who like the idea of something made here. For these businesses the local market is too small to grow on, so we focus on an online store that converts, product photography and video shot in real settings, and ad campaigns managed against margin.

cards.heading: Montana businesses we plan campaigns for

items.title: Outfitters, guides and lodging
items.text: Fishing, hunting, rafting and ranch stays are booked from afar. Search visibility, reviews and video win the booking.

items.title: Trades and contractors
items.text: Builders, roofers and heating firms need map visibility across several counties and enquiries ahead of the building season.

items.title: Healthcare
items.text: Clinics and specialists that draw patients from distant towns need clear service pages and accurate listings.

items.title: Farm and ranch supply
items.text: Equipment dealers and suppliers reach producers over wide areas with inventory pages, search and social video.

items.title: Made-in-Montana products
items.text: Gear, food and craft brands need e-commerce sites and national campaigns, since most buyers live elsewhere.

items.title: Real estate
items.text: Many buyers are relocating from other states, so listings need video, strong search presence and clear area guides.

presence: TDM works with Montana businesses remotely. We have no office or team member in the state. We meet by video call, share reports online, and deliver strategy, design, development and video as one team.

faqs.q: Does TDM have anyone on the ground in Montana?
faqs.a: No. We work with Montana businesses remotely. Calls, shared documents and regular reports keep you informed, and you supply the local knowledge and access for photos and video where needed.

faqs.q: When should a Montana tourism business start marketing for summer?
faqs.a: Earlier than most owners expect, because park trips and guided outings are planned well ahead. We look at when your past enquiries and bookings came in and start campaigns before that.

faqs.q: Is SEO worth it in a small Montana town?
faqs.a: Often yes, because there are few competitors. A complete business profile, good reviews and a clear website can make you the obvious choice for searches across a wide area at modest effort.

faqs.q: How can I sell my Montana products nationally?
faqs.a: With an online store that is easy to buy from, photography and video that show the product and where it comes from, and search and social ads tested in small steps and scaled where they pay back.

faqs.q: How much does digital marketing cost in Montana?
faqs.a: It depends on scope. We quote after a free consultation about your goals, your season and what is already in place.
